§1 — Warm-Up · Quick Fire
Can you do it? What do you need?
Activate prior knowledge · Introduce can/can't + need/want in context · Real work situations
⏱ 5–8 MIN
Skills at work
Offers & requests
Food & drinks
Office needs
💼 Quick question: Look at your job. What are 2 things you can do very well in English? (Example: "I can read emails." / "I can say hello.") Tell your partner right now.
🙋 Think about it: Your manager asks you in English: "Can you use Excel?" What do you say? What about: "Can you drive?" Try to answer — don't worry if it's not perfect!
☕ Real situation: You are in the company cafeteria. A visitor from the US asks: "Can I get a coffee here?" What do you say in English? How do you help them?
⚡ Teacher note: Collect 3–4 spontaneous answers. Don't correct yet — just notice who already knows "can" and who confuses "I can speak" with "I speak." Module 5 fixes these gaps systematically. The goal for today: by end of class every student produces "I can [verb]" and "Can I have [noun]?" naturally.
⚡ Quick Win — 20 seconds

Say this out loud right now: "I can [one real skill you have]. I need [one thing on your desk right now]." Just say it — it doesn't need to be perfect. That's today's grammar in action!

Teacher Note — Running §1

Say: "Today's module is about three power verbs: CAN, LIKE, NEED. You already use them in Spanish every day — hoy los vas a usar en inglés en tu trabajo real." Write CAN / LIKE / NEED on the board. Tell students: "By the end of this session, you will use all three in real sentences about your job."

§2 — Speaking Topic
Your Skills, Needs & Requests
3 rounds: T-S → S-S → Class · Real job context · can/can't + I need + Can I have…?
⏱ 8–10 MIN
T-S · Teacher → Student
Teacher asks each student: "Can you [skill] at work?" Students answer with "Yes, I can" or "No, I can't." Then: "What do you need for your job every day?" Student answers with: "I need [object/tool]."

"Yes, I can use Excel and I can write reports. I need a laptop and a good internet connection every day."
Target structure: can + base verb · I need + noun. No gerund — "I need working" is A2.1+.

S-S · Student — Student
Partner A asks: "Can you [skill]?" — Partner B answers and then asks a follow-up: "Can you help me with [task]?" Switch after 4 questions. Use real skills from your actual job — make it personal!

"A: 'Can you manage a team?' B: 'Yes, I can — I manage 4 people. Can you help me with the presentation slides?' A: 'Sure, no problem!'"
Colloquial target: "Sure, no problem!" — teach this as a fixed chunk now.

Class · Open Discussion
One student tells the class: "My partner can [skill] but can't [skill]. She/He needs [object] for work." Teacher: board all the "can" skills — create a class Skills Wall for the end of the module.

"My partner — Ana — can use SAP and she can speak some English. She can't drive. She needs a computer and a phone for work."
Key correction target: "She need" → "She needs" (3rd person -s). Note on board.

Teacher Note — Skills Wall

Create a "We Can…" column on the whiteboard. As Round 3 plays out, write every skill the class mentions. This becomes the vocabulary seed for §3 Vocab and reappears in S1B. Students feel proud seeing their real skills listed in English — high emotional impact, strong retention.

Teacher Note — Pronunciation: "can" vs "can't"

This is the most critical pronunciation point of M5. Say: "Listen carefully — 'can' sounds like 'cun' (weak, fast). 'Can't' sounds like 'CANT' (strong, final T)." Drill contrast: "I CAN drive" vs "I CAN'T drive." Have students hold up hand if they AGREE they can do something. Wrong stress = wrong meaning — this matters in job interviews.

§4 — Colloquial English
Sound Natural — 4 Real Phrases
Phrases native speakers use every day for offers, requests and responses · Use this week
⏱ 5 MIN
PHRASE 01
"Sure, no problem!"
The perfect response when someone asks "Can you help me?" or "Can you send me the file?" Natural, positive, professional.
A: "Can you help me with this?" B: "Sure, no problem!"
PHRASE 02
"Can I get a…?"
American English — informal way to order food or ask for something. More natural than "I want" in a cafeteria or meeting room context.
"Can I get a coffee and a sandwich, please?"
PHRASE 03
"Anything else?"
Used by the person helping you: waiter, receptionist, colleague. Your response: "No, that's all, thanks!" Learn both sides of this mini-conversation.
A: "Anything else?" B: "No, that\'s all, thanks!"
PHRASE 04
"I'm not really into [coffee]."
Polite, natural way to say you don't like something. Much better than "I don't like." Use it when someone offers you something you prefer to decline.
"Coffee? I\'m not really into coffee — I prefer tea."
Teacher Note — Drilling Colloquial

Rapid fire drill: Teacher offers something ("Coffee?") — Student responds ("Sure!" / "I'm not really into coffee."). Switch who offers. Then: "Can I get [food]?" from students at the "imaginary cafeteria counter." These 4 phrases cover 90% of cafeteria + colleague interactions. Target: zero thinking time by end of drill.

§5 — Grammar
Can / Can't · Like · Need · Want
Ability · Offers · Requests · Likes · Needs — all with nouns only at A1.1 level
⏱ 10–12 MIN
🚨 Real Work Situation

Your new American manager is visiting the Celaya plant. She asks you:
"So — what can you do? What do you like about this job? What do you need to do your work better?"

You know the answers in Spanish. But how do you say them in English — fast, professionally, without translating word by word?

✅ The Tools

"I can use SAP and I can manage the production schedule." → can + base verb
"I like this job — I like the team and the schedule." → like + noun (no "liking"!)
"I need better software. I want a new laptop." → need/want + noun
"Can I ask a question? Can you repeat that, please?" → Can I/you + base verb

StructureFormulaCorporate example
Ability (+)Subject + can + base verbI can use Excel. She can manage a team.
Ability (−)Subject + can't + base verbHe can't drive. I can't speak German.
RequestCan I + base verb + ?Can I have a coffee? Can I use your pen?
OfferCan you + base verb + ?Can you help me? Can you send the file?
LikesSubject + like + nounI like coffee. She likes salads. (NOT "liking")
NeedsSubject + need / want + nounI need a pen. He wants a new chair.
I'd like (polite)I'd like + nounI'd like a sandwich and a water, please.
⚠️ A1.1 Critical Rule — NEVER accept these at this level:
✗ "I like drinking coffee" → ✅ I like coffee (like + noun only — gerund is A2.1+)
✗ "I can to speak" → ✅ I can speak (can + base verb — no "to")
✗ "She need help" → ✅ She needs help (3rd person -s always!)
✗ "I'm can speak" → ✅ I can speak (no "am/is/are" with can)
⚡ Quick Grammar Poll — 3 Questions
1. Which is correct? Ana _____ manage a team of 10 people.
2. Which sentence is correct at A1.1 level?
3. How do you ask politely for a coffee at the cafeteria?
✏️ Activity A — Complete the Sentence
Teacher Note — Activity A

Run as rapid-fire oral drill first. Teacher shows the incomplete sentence. Students shout the answer before clicking. Then confirm by clicking. This gets students speaking before interacting with the screen.

1. She _____ use SAP — she learned it last year. (habilidad positiva)
2. "_____ I borrow your charger? My phone is at 3%."
3. I _____ coffee — I prefer tea. (no me gusta)
4. He _____ a pen and a notebook for the training session.
5. _____ you send me the report by 5 PM? (petición)
✏️ Activity B — Grammar Rules: True or False?
"I like drinking coffee" is correct A1.1 English.
"Can I have a water, please?" is a correct and polite request.
"She can to drive" is correct. The word "to" is needed after can.
"He need a pen" is correct — 'need' doesn't change for he/she/it.
"I'd like a sandwich" is a polite and natural way to order food in English.
🗣️ Micro-Speaking: Tell your partner 2 real things: "I can [skill] but I can't [skill]." Then: "I like [noun]. I need [noun] right now." 45 seconds each.
§6 — Listening
Skills Interview — Ana at Vertex Logistics
Ana García describes her skills and needs in a real work conversation · Listen for can/can't + I need
⏱ 8–10 MIN
Skills & Needs Interview — Vertex Logistics, Celaya
A1.1 · M5 · S1A · Voice: Lauren (ElevenLabs) · Real Audio
0:00 --:--
Hi! My name is Ana García. I'm a coordinator at Vertex Logistics here in Celaya, Guanajuato.

In my job, I can use Excel — I use it every day for the schedules and the reports. I can also write emails in English — not perfect, but I can communicate! I can drive, so I can visit our clients in Querétaro and Irapuato.

What can't I do? Well, I can't speak French — only Spanish and a little English. And I can't use Photoshop or design software. I'm not a designer!

I like my job. I like the team — they are friendly and helpful. I like the schedule too — I start at eight and I finish at five.

What do I need? For my work, I need a good laptop, a fast internet connection, and a comfortable chair — I sit all day! I also need coffee. A lot of coffee!

Oh — and I'd like a new notebook. My current one is almost full. Can you help me find one in the supply room? That's all — thanks!
📎 ElevenLabs: Voice — Sarah (American English) · Speed 0.78 · Pitch 1.0 · ~155 words · A1.1 M5 S1A
Teacher Note — Pre-Listening Task

Before playing, say: "Listen for 3 things Ana CAN do. Listen for 1 thing she CAN'T do. Listen for 2 things she NEEDS." Students hold up 1, 2, or 3 fingers as they hear each category. This keeps listening active, not passive. Second listen: note vocabulary. Third (optional): read along with script.

✏️ Comprehension — Multiple Choice
1. What can Ana do at work? Select the correct answer.
2. What does Ana need for her work? Select the correct answer.
✏️ Listening — True or False
Ana can speak French and a little English.
Ana likes her team — she says they are friendly.
Ana wants a new pen. Her current one is almost empty.
Ana works at a company in Celaya, Guanajuato.
🗣️ From memory: Close the script. Tell your partner in 2 sentences: what CAN Ana do? What does she NEED? Try to remember — don't look!
§7 — Production
Your Skills, Your Needs — Real Talk
Opinion Meter · Speaking challenges · 60-second cafeteria role-play · Timer challenge
⏱ 12–15 MIN
"I can do my job completely in English right now — no Spanish needed."
Disagree50 / 50Agree
50%
Teacher Note — Opinion Meter Use

After the class votes, ask: "Who pressed Agree? Tell us why." "Who pressed Disagree? What can't you do in English yet?" This generates authentic production with can/can't. Perfect warm-up for the speaking cards below. Students defend their position = real argument with target grammar.

Question 1 — T-S · Your Work Skills
Tell the teacher 3 things you can do at work in English. Then 1 thing you can't do yet. Use real skills from your actual job — no invented answers!
💡 "I can [verb]... I can also [verb]... but I can't [verb] yet."
Question 2 — S-S · The Skills Interview
Partner A plays the manager. Partner B plays the new employee. Manager asks: "Can you [skill]?" Employee answers honestly. Then switch roles. 4 questions each — use the vocab from today.
💡 Manager: "Can you drive? Can you speak English? Can you use Excel?" Employee: "Yes, I can" / "No, I can't — but I can [alternative]."
Question 3 — Cafeteria Role Play 🍽️
Partner A = cafeteria worker. Partner B = employee ordering lunch. Order 2 items, ask the price (from M1: "How much is it?"), respond to "Anything else?", say thank you and goodbye. 90 seconds per pair. Switch roles.
💡 B: "Can I get a coffee and a sandwich, please?" A: "Sure! Anything else?" B: "No, that\'s all, thanks!"
Question 4 — Class · My Colleague Needs…
After interviewing your partner, tell the class: "My colleague [name] can [skill]. She/He needs [object] for work. She/He likes [thing]." Teacher: note every 3rd-person -s error. Correct warmly but immediately.
💡 Watch for: "She need" → "She needs" / "He like" → "He likes"
⭐ 60-Second Challenge — Skills Pitch
Teacher Note — 60-Second Challenge

One student at a time. Set the timer. They must say: 3 things they can do, 1 thing they can't, 1 thing they like, 1 thing they need — all in English, no Spanish, no stopping. Partner counts how many verbs they use. This is preparation for the S5 exit task. Award badge b3 for completing it.

Speak for 60 seconds about your real work skills. Include: 3 "can" sentences, 1 "can't", 1 "I like", 1 "I need". No Spanish. No stopping. GO!
Use: I can [verb] · I can't [verb] · I like [noun] · I need [noun]

I can say what I can and can't do at work: "I can use Excel. I can't speak French."
I can make polite requests: "Can I have a coffee, please?" / "Can you help me?"

🎯 3 Phrases for This Week — Use them at work starting tomorrow
PHRASE 1
"Can I get a [coffee], please?"
Use this in the cafeteria, at a meeting, or when visiting a client's office. It's the most natural way to order or ask for something in American English. Replaces "I want" in professional contexts.
PHRASE 2
"Sure, no problem!"
Use this every time a colleague or client asks "Can you help me?" or "Can you send the file?" It's positive, professional, and completely natural. Use it today — it works 100% of the time.
PHRASE 3
"I can [skill] but I can't [skill]."
Use this in any introduction, job interview, or team meeting when someone asks about your skills. Direct, honest, professional. "I can manage schedules but I can't speak French yet." Perfect.
